summary: Shasta National Forest lookout on Mt. Bradley near Dunsmuir; NHLR gives 1933 build, newspapers show 1930-32 start, staffed into the 1960s, tramway threat.

facts.design: USFS R1 cabin on a 13-foot enclosed timber tower

staffing.status: historically staffed; no later staffing found in the sources read

facts.agency: US Forest Service, Shasta-Trinity National Forest

events.note: Shasta National Forest announced a lookout station on Mt. Bradley just west of Dunsmuir
Lookout house completed by July 1932, per a Searchlight item reprinted on the Forest Lookouts page; NHLR gives 1933
NHLR build year for the USFS R1 cabin on a 13-foot enclosed timber tower
Frank Bascom named lookout for the season
Mt. Bradley the first lookout manned that season; only station with direct telephone contact to USFS headquarters
October damage to shutters, a window and roof shingles; described as minor compared with Black Butte
Lightning struck a tree near the cabin; the lookout was knocked to the floor, per her own account
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register

evidence.supports: Built 1933 as a USFS R1 cabin on a 13-foot enclosed timber tower
evidence.quote: Mount Bradley was built for the Shasta National Forest in 1933, a USFS R1 cabin atop a 13 foot enclosed timber tower.

evidence.supports: Administered by the Shasta-Trinity National Forest, US Forest Service
evidence.quote: US Forest Service - Shasta-Trinity National Forest

evidence.supports: Structure is maintained but threatened by a proposed aerial tramway project
evidence.quote: The structure is being maintained but is under threat from a proposed aerial tramway project.

evidence.supports: Registered on the NHLR on April 16, 2020
July 1930 announcement of a lookout station on Mt. Bradley just west of Dunsmuir
evidence.quote: Ever on the alert to detect forest fires before they become uncontrollable, the Shasta national forest is establishing a lookout station on Mt. Bradley just west of Dunsmuir.

evidence.supports: Past fires in the Sacramento River canyon had caused firefighting trouble
evidence.quote: During past years forest fires in the Sacramento river canyon in this vicinity have caused forest fire fighting no little trouble

evidence.supports: By July 1932 a lookout house was complete so a lookout could live on the peak that summer
evidence.quote: L. T. Solaro and C. W. Durst have completed a lookout house on Mt. Bradley, where the lookout can reside during his stay on the peak this summer.

evidence.supports: Frank Bascom named the lookout for the 1943 season
evidence.quote: He will be the look-out on Mt. Bradley for the season.

evidence.supports: In 1956 Mt. Bradley was the first lookout manned that season
evidence.quote: Mt. Bradley was the first lookout to be manned.

evidence.supports: Only station with direct telephone contact to Forest Service headquarters
evidence.quote: The Bradley lookout is the key lookout for this area, being the only one with direct telephone communication with USFS headquarters.

evidence.supports: Pearl Cowen spent summers on Mt. Bradley around 1960
evidence.quote: Pearl Cowen, veteran fire lookout, who spends her summers on Mt. Bradley, is in a Chico hospital recovering from recent surgery.

evidence.supports: Pearl Cowen was in charge at Mt. Bradley in 1962
evidence.quote: A veteran look-out is Pearl Cowen, in charge at Mt. Bradley.

evidence.supports: The October 1962 damage was minor compared with Black Butte
evidence.quote: In describing the damage to the lookout on Mt. Bradley, it was rather minor in comparison with that at Black Butte.

evidence.supports: Damage was two shutters gone, a broken window and some roof shingles lost
evidence.quote: Two of the shutter are gone, one window broken and some of the shingles from the roof.

evidence.supports: Lightning struck a tree near the cabin in June 1963
evidence.quote: see that tree that has been struck by lightning?

evidence.supports: The lightning strike knocked the lookout to the floor
evidence.quote: The impact of the strike knocked me flat on the floor.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR gives 1933 as the build year. A 1932 Searchlight item reprinted on the Forest Lookouts page says a lookout house was completed by July 1932. The story keeps both dates and does not pick one.

notes_for_editor: Access and rental status are not established: the NHLR page says only that the structure is maintained and faces a proposed tramway. Search snippets (not fetched, not cited) mention a road from Dunsmuir and a hike to the tower; check before publishing any access claim. The Mount Shasta News article returned HTTP 403. The Forest Lookouts newspaper items end in June 1963. The lookout's name appears as Cown (1956, 1959), Cowen (1960, 1962) and Cowan (1963) across the items, and the story uses Cowen. The brief's record (built 1933, standing, NHLR registration 2020) is consistent with the NHLR page; no corrections proposed.
